decisions.quote: We previously performed data‐driven classification based on large‐scale neuroimaging datasets to identify a potential novel subtype of psychiatric disorders characterized by the pronounced enlarged ventricles and cognitive impairment (EVCI) in one cohort. However, these findings have yet to be validated across independent cohorts. Herein, we investigated the availability of cognitive data in other cohorts in the Cognitive Genetics Collaborative Research Organization (COCORO) project to assess the presence of cognitive impairment (CI).
decisions.reason: The paper re-tests the previously published EVCI subtype classification using cognitive and ventricular data from eight independent cohorts not included in the original single-cohort EVCI analysis.

corrected_value.title: Proposal for a Novel Classification of Patients With Enlarged Ventricles and Cognitive Impairment Based on Data‐Driven Analysis of Neuroimaging Results in Patients With Psychiatric Disorders
corrected_value.authors: Yasuda, Y., Ito, S., Matsumoto, J., et al.

decisions.quote: In our previous study [ 6 ], we performed data‐driven classification based on large‐scale neuroimaging datasets to identify a novel subtype of psychiatric disorders characterized by pronounced EV and CI (i.e., EVCI).
decisions.reason: The replicated study is reference [6] (10.1002/npr2.70010), which first identified the EVCI subtype in the Osaka University cohort, whereas the shipped target reference [19] (10.1002/npr2.70029) is a clinical case series cited only in the discussion as supporting background.

decisions.quote: This study validated the existence of the EVCI subgroup in independent cohorts, thus supporting our previous findings.
decisions.reason: The authors state an explicit overall verdict that the existence and characteristics of the EVCI subgroup from reference [6] were validated and supported in independent cohorts.
